bullets.title: S&P 500 hits new all-time high at 7,800; equal-weight RSP also at record
bullets.body: The S&P 500 crossed above 7,800 for the first time, its 9th 100-point milestone of the year (was 6,400 one year ago, 4,400 five years ago). Nasdaq 100 rose 1%, S&P +0.6%, while the equal-weight RSP also reached all-time highs, suggesting broadening market participation. VIX plunged below 15 to 2026 lows, and SPY hit $5B+ call walls at 775 and 780 strikes.

bullets.title: July PPI cooler than expected across the board; rate-hike odds fade
bullets.body: US producer prices came in flat (0.0% MoM vs. +0.2% est.) in July with YoY PPI at +4.7% vs. +4.9% expected; core PPI +0.2% MoM vs. +0.3% est. Following yesterday's CPI beat, the back-to-back disinflation data points caused markets to sharply pare rate-hike expectations. BofA economists had forecast 3 hikes in 2026, while prediction markets now show 70% odds of a Fed hold in September and only 29% for a 25bp hike.

bullets.title: Fed's Barkin and Hammack signal divergent views; hikes technically still on the table
bullets.body: Richmond Fed's Barkin says rate hikes remain an open question, noting sticky price pressures may require either weaker demand or tightening to hit 2% — but also says 'many' FOMC members view current rates as sufficient. Cleveland Fed's Hammack was more hawkish, explicitly calling to act now and raising rates, citing broad-based inflation and policy that is not yet restrictive. Barkin flagged federal debt as an inflationary 'wind' the Fed must navigate against.

bullets.title: US posts record July budget deficit of $432B; national debt hits $39.94T
bullets.body: The US federal government posted a record $432B July budget deficit, driven by rising Medicare costs and interest payments. National debt has reached $39.94T, with the current fiscal year deficit already exceeding the entire prior year total by August.

bullets.title: 30-year Treasury auction clears at 5.216%, highest yield since 2001
bullets.body: The $25B 30-year bond auction drew a 5.216% yield — highest since 2001 — with a 0.4bp tail to the when-issued. Bid-to-cover was 2.39; indirect bidders took 66.8%, direct bidders 21.6%, primary dealers just 11.5%.

bullets.title: Initial jobless claims rose to 209K, above 202K forecast; continuing claims fall
bullets.body: Initial claims for the week ending Aug 8 increased 9K to 209K, above the 202K survey estimate (prior revised down to 200K). Continuing claims fell 22K to 1.777M vs. 1.794M expected — near 2-year lows — suggesting the labor market remains healthy despite the headline miss. Largest state increases in Michigan, New York, and Texas.

bullets.title: CreditSights: Fed holds rates through H1 2027; BofA still forecasts 3 hikes in 2026
bullets.body: CreditSights forecasts the Fed could keep rates unchanged through all of 2026 and into the first half of 2027. In contrast, Bank of America economists reiterated expectations for three rate increases in 2026. The divergence reflects ongoing uncertainty around whether the current disinflation trend is durable.

bullets.title: Strait of Hormuz tensions escalate; oil pulls back after 5-session rally
bullets.body: Iran claimed full control of the Strait of Hormuz, stating no vessel can transit without approval; the US asserts it can maintain its blockade indefinitely and is deploying a fresh aircraft carrier to the region. Despite the rhetoric, WTI fell below $82 and Brent dropped to ~$87.67 as traders took profits and US crude inventories rose 17.4M barrels. The IEA estimates a 1.8M bpd global oil shortfall this quarter, while commercial traffic through Hormuz remains in single digits in both directions.

bullets.title: Diesel crack spread hits all-time high above $98 on Houthi refinery attack
bullets.body: Diesel cracks surged to a record above $98/barrel after reports that Yemen's Houthis attacked Saudi Aramco's Jizan Refinery with two drones. US Strategic Petroleum Reserve also fell below 300M barrels for the first time since January 1983, adding to refined-products supply anxiety.

bullets.title: Tech earnings guidance-raise rate running at 2.3x historical average
bullets.body: Nearly one-third (33%) of Tech stocks that have reported earnings this season raised guidance, vs. a 25-year historical average of 14% — a 2.3x premium. Health Care, Real Estate, and Industrials are also raising guidance at roughly double historical rates, suggesting broad earnings momentum.

bullets.title: AAII sentiment: bears slightly outnumber bulls; bull/bear spread stays tight
bullets.body: The latest AAII investor sentiment survey shows bears slightly outnumber bulls, with the bull/bear spread remaining tight over the past year. The last significant bearish spike was February–May 2025. The restrained sentiment backdrop may limit near-term contrarian catalyst from a sentiment washout.

bullets.title: Japan government backs another BoJ rate hike as soon as September–October
bullets.body: Japan's government reportedly supports another Bank of Japan rate hike with potential timing of September or October. A BoJ hike would strengthen the yen and could revive carry-trade unwind dynamics relevant to global tech/semi positioning.

bullets.title: Canada–US tariff deadline August 19 approaches; automakers warn $2B+ cost impact
bullets.body: Canada–US trade discussions have 'heated up' ahead of an August 19 tariff deadline, with Saskatchewan Premier Scott Moe emphasizing focus on renewing CUSMA. Separately, Detroit automakers are warning the White House that proposed content rules requiring 50% US-made parts could add at least $2B per automaker annually.

bullets.title: Anthropic investors eye $2T+ valuation and potential October IPO at $120B ARR run rate
bullets.body: Anthropic investors are betting on a $2T+ valuation in a potential October IPO that could be the largest stock market debut ever. Separately, backers project annualized revenue could reach $100B–$120B by year-end. One commentator noted the $3T in OpenAI/Anthropic funding commitments rests on an assumption that frontier model pricing remains stable — a risk if costs decline.

bullets.title: AMD prices $5B debt deal — potentially its largest ever — to fund AI expansion
bullets.body: AMD plans to raise up to $5B through a four-part bond sale to fund AI-related capital spending, including major agreements with Anthropic and Microsoft. Separately, $2M+ in 1DTE call options on NVDA and AMD hit the tape, flagged as unusual bullish positioning.

bullets.title: US-Israel joint military operations may resume; CENTCOM pushes for Iran infrastructure strikes
bullets.body: CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper has reportedly pushed for renewed strikes on Iran's gas, oil, and electricity infrastructure, and has told senior IDF officials joint military operations may resume. The US has also established a new drone task force and has lost ~25% of its Reaper drone fleet (45 MQ-9s, ~$1.3B+) during the Iran conflict.

bullets.title: DeepSeek raises model prices 4x+, moving closer to competitor pricing
bullets.body: DeepSeek is raising prices on its V4-Flash model from $0.28 to $1.32 per million output tokens during peak hours effective August 16, representing a 4x+ increase. The move suggests the era of aggressively below-market AI pricing from Chinese open-source providers may be moderating.

bullets.title: U.S. private credit default rate at record high; 30Y auction shows weak demand
bullets.body: Fitch reports the US private credit default rate remained at a record high in July 2026. The weak 30Y Treasury auction — highest yield since 2001 with a tail — adds to concerns about the durability of credit conditions underpinning leveraged buyouts and AI infrastructure debt.

bullets.title: AI productivity ROI debate intensifies; Morgan Stanley stays bullish
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley reiterated its bullish stance on AI. But contrarian pushback is growing: one analyst argues AI has not yet driven measurable end-customer revenue growth or productivity gains, and that the $3T in OpenAI/Anthropic funding assumes stable frontier pricing. BofA noted AI is currently inflationary rather than productivity-enhancing.

bullets.title: Fitch: private credit and AI bubble among top macro risks to watch
bullets.body: Fed's Hammack explicitly flagged 'watch private credit' and 'whether AI is a bubble' as key monitoring items. Elevated leverage in Treasury purchases and record-high private credit defaults add to systemic risk concerns outside the equity tape.
